title: Toward Automated Detection of Portability Bugs in Kokkos Parallel Programs
problem: Programs written in performance-portable frameworks like Kokkos may contain portability bugs that only manifest on specific hardware backends (CUDA, HIP, OpenMP). Traditional testing cannot effectively discover these bugs as it would require concrete execution on all supported hardware configurations for potentially infinite input sets.
motivation: Detecting portability bugs before deployment on supercomputers enables broader hardware support and reduces development time.
method: The approach categorizes the types of portability bugs that appear in Kokkos programs—bugs that only manifest when code runs on specific hardware backends like CUDA GPUs, HIP (AMD's parallel computing platform), or OpenMP CPUs. Klokkos, a tool developed for this work, uses symbolic execution (a technique that tests code against many possible inputs simultaneously without actually running it) to detect these bugs on regular commodity hardware. This enables early bug detection before code deployment to supercomputers, avoiding failures that would only appear on those specific hardware systems.
key_novelty: The core idea is using symbolic execution—a technique that explores code without actually running it—to find portability bugs in Kokkos programs on commodity hardware, without needing to test on the specific hardware backends (CUDA, HIP, OpenMP) where they would occur.
contributions: Categorization of common portability bugs in Kokkos parallel programs
Klokkos static analysis tool based on symbolic execution for portability bug detection
Demonstration that static analysis can detect all identified bugs with zero false positives
Proof-of-concept showing efficiency on commodity hardware before supercomputer deployment
limitations: Preliminary proof-of-concept; evaluated only on identified bug categories and small examples; scalability to large real-world Kokkos programs not demonstrated.
primary_theme: portability bug detection via static analysis
